lines.quote: Designed and implemented digital beamforming algorithms for Boreal’s 64-element silicon-photonic beam steering prototype.
Wrote the real-time DSP firmware in C for Boreal’s photodetector readout evaluation board (ARM Cortex-M4 target).
Own and maintain Boreal’s internal calibration data pipeline — approx. 15k lines, fully unit-tested (pytest), CI/CD via GitLab, used daily by the 20-person engineering team.

Conducted regular RF characterisation of photodetector front-end electronics using Rohde & Schwarz ZVL vector network analysers and Keysight N9020A spectrum analysers; responsible for gain flatness and noise-figure verification on incoming sensor modules.

requirements.name: Relevant degree or demonstrated equivalent

lines.quote: I believe that demonstrated competence is at least as valid as a degree in the right field, and I think my track record makes the case clearly.

requirements.note: The named degree field (Materials Science and Engineering) does not match the requirement's listed fields; status reflects the cover letter's explicit demonstrated-equivalent-competence argument together with the concrete production, embedded, RF and publication evidence recorded elsewhere in this application. Field relevance is left for the recruiter to judge.

lines.quote: Since 2022, leading a four-person signal processing subteam responsible for Boreal’s next-generation sensor readout architecture. Hiring, sprint planning, code review, and technical direction.
V. Jarvinen et al., “Adaptive interference suppression in irregular optical phased arrays,” SESE Transactions on Signal Processing, vol. 70, 2022.
All work conducted in English (Boreal’s working language); quarterly progress presentations to international customers including two Japanese optics firms and a German automotive tier-1.

Coordinated a three-month sensor integration and field-test campaign at Boreal’s Oulu facility. Relocated from the Helsinki office for the project; remained at the Oulu site and have been based there since.
